positions.commentary: The speaker views Amazon as an exceptional business with high returns on equity and a long runway, justifying a 'go all in' investment strategy.
Nick Sleep's portfolio was heavily concentrated in Costco along with Amazon and Berkshire Hathaway.
The speaker does not understand 99% of the world, including Google, and only needs to understand what he invests in.

thesis: This episode argues that investors should focus on businesses they deeply understand rather than trying to comprehend the entire world, citing Amazon and Costco as exceptional companies with high returns on equity and long runways. It also expresses a bearish view on Bitcoin due to its speculative nature and includes a personal bullish stance on the Turkey business based on good management.

claims.claim: Nick Sleep held a massive position in Amazon before shutting down his funds, demonstrating deep understanding of the business.
claims.quote: In 2013, when he was, just before he shut down his funds, he was running about $3 billion in capital. And 40% of the capital was invested in Amazon. So about $1.2 billion was in Amazon stock.

claims.claim: Nick Sleep's portfolio was heavily concentrated in Costco along with Amazon and Berkshire Hathaway.
claims.quote: And then Costco and Berksha Hathaway made up almost the rest of the portfolio. So 90% of the portfolio was Amazon Costco and Berksha happening.

claims.claim: The speaker does not understand 99% of the world, including Google, and only needs to understand what he invests in.
claims.quote: So the thing is that 99%, of the stuff that goes on in this world, I do not understand. And that's perfectly fine, because I only need to understand things that I actually invest in.

claims.claim: The speaker would not hold Bitcoin if forced to choose between buying or selling it due to speculative elements.
claims.quote: If you were to ask me, I only have two choices buy Bitcoin or sell Bitcoin, I would not want to be holding Bitcoin. I think that there are a number of speculative elements associated with it.

claims.claim: The speaker views Amazon as an exceptional business with high returns on equity and a long runway, justifying a 'go all in' investment strategy.
claims.quote: he understood Amazon really well. He did not want to change even 10 years from now his Amazon position because he understood that business was exceptional.

claims.claim: The speaker owns one third of the Turkey business and plans to keep it for a long time due to good managers and liking the business.
claims.quote: We own one third of that business, which means that out of the 12 million square feet, 4 million square feet belongs to us, my fund investors. I like that business. The managers are really good. And we will keep that business for a long time.
